source.author: Matthew Durrant
source.title: Aeroelastic Instability of Reduced-scale High-altitude Pseudo-satellite Wings

conventions.incidence_mapping: Vertical +z wing, chord +x and normal -y; positive section incidence is body beta.
conventions.comparison_observables: Published ASWING linear flutter boundary and individual experimental destruction speeds remain separate.
conventions.baseline_choices: Main-table mass/stiffness, no concentrated objects, gravity -z at 9.805 m/s², density 1.225 kg/m³, fixed PG Mach zero. These are explicit reconstruction choices, not a recovered original ASWING setup.

unresolved: Appendix A is labelled UNCORRELATED and has different stiffness, inertia distributions and elastic-axis locations from Tables 2.20 and 3.5-3.7. No evidence establishes which exact input generated Tables 4.1-4.2.
Appendix Weight comments put Ixx/Iyy/Izz/Ixy immediately after Mg. The public ASWING guide instead puts CDA/Vol/Hx/Hy/Hz before inertia. No undocumented positional mapping is assumed.
Section 3.10 prose gives Nea=0.005 m, while Table 3.7 and both appendices give 0.001 m. The table reconstruction uses 0.001 m with the conflict retained.
Reported zero-airspeed ASWING modes do not specify whether quiescent-air apparent mass and gravity preload were active, or the exact numerical mesh.

GVT used a temporarily taped accelerometer and suspended lead wire (section 2.2.13); their mass and attachment are not specified there. Appendix F separately describes two tip accelerometers on additional wings. These may not be substituted for the GVT apparatus.
Nominal 75-percent spar position is not the elastic-axis coordinate. Table 2.20 reports Xax=0.3844; the appendix uses 0.3663.

Flutter airspeed in the experiment is defined by catastrophic structural failure, while a linear eigenvalue crossing describes onset of local instability; these observables are not automatically equivalent.
Tables 3.8-3.10 print positive CLmin for no-stall limits; the pilot uses the unambiguous Case 4 table instead of silently changing signs.
Exact published mesh, wake options, gravity and PG settings remain unrecorded. Sensitivity checks are required before interpreting a boundary discrepancy.
